description: We are Information Systems students interested in data analysis, technology, and environmental sustainability. We focus on data exploration, visualization, and turning satellite data into meaningful insights. Our areas of interest include Python, data science, GIS, remote sensing, and web development.
summary:
Kalender Gambut is an interactive geospatial dashboard designed to make satellite-detected hotspot observations and burned-area information easier to explore in Central Kalimantan, Indonesia. It combines NASA FIRMS active fire detections from MODIS and VIIRS with administrative and selected Peat Hydrological Unit (KHG) boundaries, alongside annual burned-area information from Indonesia’s SiPongi system.

Users can filter hotspot observations by year and satellite sensor, explore their spatial distribution on an interactive map, and examine regional and annual patterns through charts and data tables covering 14 administrative regions. By bringing these different datasets into one accessible platform, Kalender Gambut helps students, researchers, and environmental stakeholders explore peatland fire activity and its geographic context. It is an exploratory monitoring and information tool, not a real-time fire warning or ground-confirmation system.
details:
Kalender Gambut is an interactive web-based geospatial dashboard for exploring satellite-detected hotspot observations and burned-area information in Central Kalimantan, Indonesia.

The application consists of three main sections:

1. Hotspot Map: Displays the spatial distribution of MODIS and VIIRS hotspot detections. Users can filter observations by year and satellite sensor and explore their geographic locations in relation to administrative and selected peatland boundaries.

2. Regional Analysis and Burned Area: Provides annual and regional data visualizations, including hotspot statistics and burned-area information from SiPongi. Users can examine data across 14 administrative regions through interactive charts and tables.

3. About Data: Provides information about the datasets and sources used in the application.

The project integrates satellite observations from NASA FIRMS with geographic boundary datasets and annual burned-area information from SiPongi.

The datasets are prepared and organized using Python and Pandas. Geographic information is represented using GeoJSON boundary layers, while PyDeck is used for geospatial map visualization and Plotly is used for interactive charts.

Users interact with the dashboard by selecting years and satellite sensors, exploring hotspot distributions, and examining regional summaries.

Kalender Gambut aims to make satellite-based hotspot information more accessible and easier to understand.

Its intended benefits include:

• Improving access to satellite-derived hotspot observations.

• Helping users explore spatial and temporal patterns of hotspot detections.

• Providing geographic context through peat hydrological and administrative boundaries.

• Supporting comparisons of hotspot observations and burned-area information across regions and years.

• Encouraging environmental awareness and data-driven exploration of peatland fire activity.

The project is intended as an exploratory monitoring and information platform. It does not replace official fire reports, field verification, or emergency response systems.

The project's main creative approach is integrating multiple data sources into a single interactive geospatial interface.

Instead of presenting satellite observations, geographic boundaries, and burned-area statistics separately, Kalender Gambut brings them together to support easier regional exploration.

Important considerations include differences in MODIS and VIIRS spatial resolution, the distinction between satellite-detected thermal anomalies and confirmed fires, and the need to distinguish hotspot detections from reported burned-area measurements.

Tools and Technologies

• Programming language: Python.

• Web application framework: Streamlit.

• Data processing: Pandas and NumPy.

• Interactive charts: Plotly.

• Geospatial visualization: PyDeck.

• Geographic operations: Shapely.

• Geographic data format: GeoJSON.

• Development environment: Google Colab.

• Source code management: GitHub.

• Application hosting: Streamlit Community Cloud.

No specialized hardware is required to use the web dashboard.
